# D-30: Modules are the source; the app's module regions are generated

**Status:** Proposed (Matt to approve). Implemented on `claude/modular-component-architecture-kzv0i7` (TD-245, TEST-81).
**Directed by:** Matt, 2026-10-02. He asked for components with discrete inputs and outputs to be developed, versioned and tested as standalone files, then merged into the single file when they work, and to be reusable in other apps.

## Decision

`src/modules/<id>/` is the only place a module is edited. Its region in `src/milestone-dashboard.html` is output, written by `tools/modules_embed.py` between named markers, and never edited by hand. `src/modules/MODULES.json` is the index of every module: its version, files, global, dependencies, tests, and position in the app.

This is the **amalgamation** pattern: the same model SQLite uses to ship `sqlite3.c`, and stb and Dear ImGui use for single-header libraries. Many source files are the truth, and one file is the deliverable. The app still has no build step: the paste is a dev-time copy of unchanged text. `tools/grid_view_embed.py` already did this for the grid view from P70, and this decision generalises it.

## Industry patterns compared

| Pattern | What it gives | Taken here |
|---|---|---|
| Amalgamation (SQLite, stb, ImGui) | Modular sources, single-file deliverable | **Yes: the core model** |
| Vendoring with provenance (Go `vendor/`, our `vendor/<lib>/SOURCE.md`, Claude-General `skills/` `source:` block) | Copy, pin and record where it came from | **Yes: for reuse in other apps** (below) |
| Component-driven development (Storybook, Bit) | Build and test a component in isolation | **Yes:** module tests plus the `prototypes/grid-view/` harness |
| Contract testing (Pact) | Each side tests the interface on its own | **Yes:** `INTERFACE.md` or the source header is the contract, with the module's own test |
| Per-package semver and tags (monorepo tools such as Changesets) | Each component has its own version | **Yes:** a version per module in `MODULES.json`, and a tag per integrated release |
| ES modules plus a bundler; git submodules or subtree | Native imports; a shared repo per component | **No.** A bundler breaks the no-build constraint. Submodules add a second repo and a checkout step for a single-file app with one consumer today |

## The mechanism

**Markers.** Each embedded module has a pair of lines per kind (js, css) that carry its id, its version, and a hash of the text between them:

```
// @module notes-store js 1.0.0 sha256=<16 hex> BEGIN: generated by tools/modules_embed.py from src/modules/notes-store/, do not edit here
...banner, source unchanged, end banner...
// @module notes-store js END
```

The tool replaces only the text between a module's own pair. This closes TD-238, where the grid re-paste rewrote everything from its banner to `</style>` and removed a neighbouring block.

**Slots** (`// @slot app-script-modules`, `/* @slot style-modules */`) mark where a newly embedded module is inserted. Within a slot, `order` in the manifest is the load order, and `--check` fails if the app disagrees with it.

**Findings** from `--check`:

| Finding | Meaning |
|---|---|
| TAMPERED | The region in the app was edited by hand. `--embed` refuses to overwrite it. |
| STALE | The source or manifest changed since the last embed. |
| UNVERSIONED | A source changed and its version did not. |
| MISSING | An embedded module has no region in the app. |
| STRAY | The app has a region for a module the manifest does not embed. |
| MISMATCH | A module folder has no manifest entry, or the reverse. |

**Versions.**
- **One version per module, written once.** The `version` field in `MODULES.json` holds it, and the marker reads from it. This is the same single-source rule as `APP_VERSION`.
- **Semver levels:** major means the interface changed, and needs a migration note plus the app adapter updated in the same change. Minor is additive. Patch is a fix.
- **Starting versions:** a module is 1.0.0 when it is first embedded in a release. Standalone modules start at 0.1.0.
- **What the tool records:** the version and source hashes at the last embed, in a `recorded` block, which is how it detects UNVERSIONED.

**Tags.** When a release carries a changed module, the release commit gets an annotated tag for that module as well as the app tag: `p6md/<id>/v<x.y.z>`. Tags are cut by a person at release, never by an agent (Governance 02).

**Extraction.** `--extract <id> --js-lines A-B [--css-lines C-D]` lifts app lines into `src/modules/<id>/` unchanged, leaving markers behind. Afterwards the app differs only by the marker lines. Turning the lifted code into a clean module (one IIFE, one global, no app globals read) is a follow-up change to the module file, versioned like any other.

## Testing: what this saves, and what it does not

- **During development (the saving):** a module is tested alone: its Node test, its harness check, or the prototype. That takes seconds, needs no app and no Chromium, and is repeated as often as needed.
- **At integration:** `--embed`, then `tools/run_checks.py`, which selects checks by changed region (`docs/check-map.md`).
  - **Limit, measured at TEST-81:** the region map treats a module's IIFE as one top-level chunk, and every chunk runs at load. So embedding any module change re-selects every browser check that loads the app.
  - **What this means:** integration is one full run per module merge, not one per edit. The saving is in how many full runs are needed, not in how big each one is.
  - **Follow-up:** narrowing the selection needs function-level regions inside module IIFEs (TD-246).

## Reuse in other apps

The route already exists in the hub, and nothing new is enacted here:

1. **Promote.** A module that meets R1 to R8 of `Governance/04-resource-governance.md` on `main-projects-hub` is promoted to `Resources/Components/<id>/`, with its `RESOURCE.md` and a catalogue row.
2. **Copy.** A consuming app copies the module folder at a tag and records `source:` (repo, path, ref, sha256), as `vendor/<lib>/SOURCE.md` does today.
3. **No auto-propagation.** The `RESOURCE.md` "Known copies" list says who to tell when a new version ships.

A tenancy-wide standard for single-file amalgamation is proposed separately in Claude-General `recommendations/register.md` (P-25). This file does not depend on it.

## Rejected

- **Hand-pasting with banners only (the pre-D-30 state).** It has no version, no tamper check, and greedy boundaries (TD-238).
- **A `VERSION` constant inside each module's source.** It would put code into the app for a value that only tooling reads. The manifest is the one place instead.
- **Per-module repos or submodules.** They add overhead with no second consumer today. Revisit once a module is promoted and a second app copies it.
